clue.text: Cave if fool goes berserk in leader's workplace

indicators.note: going berserk means running wild, so the letters of these three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells a fool to cave in, and the fool runs riot inside the boss's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes berserk' rearranges CAVE IF FOOL; 'in' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The President of the United States, a national leader, works in this oval-shaped room in the White House.

clue.text: Evict rogues regularly behind in rent

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word rogues, here the second, fourth and sixth
the behind of a word is its rear end, so this takes the final letter of rent

explanation.surface: A landlord throws out tenants who are crooks and are behind with their rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes OUS from rogues; 'behind in' gives the last letter of rent, T. The surface reads 'behind in rent' as being in arrears.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict someone is to force them out of a property, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Some dread a man temping for firm

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people fear having a man come in to temp for their company.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition was 'for firm'; 'for' is a link word, and the definition is just 'firm', which matches the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant is unshakeable in their view, so firm is a close synonym.

clue.text: Writings that could become modest talent

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could become something else when rearranged, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Pieces of writing which might turn a modest talent into something greater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that could become' rearranges MODEST TALENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The first part of the Christian Bible is a collection of sacred writings, from Genesis onwards.

clue.text: Important part of body tires first

indicators.note: first puts the word for tires ahead of the body part

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken
the hip is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A key bit of the body is the first to grow weary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is the charade's order signal, not part of the definition. 'Important' is used as an adjective, as in a flagship store.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, a flagship product or store is the leading, most significant one of its kind.

clue.text: Jokers and clubs depressed bridge partners

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
depressed means low in spirits
in bridge, North and South are partners at the table

explanation.surface: Pranksters and a card club's gloomy bridge pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points; North and South play as one pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowns are people who play the fool and crack jokes, so jokers fits well.

clue.text: Sailor the Spanish portrayed as murder victim

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish sailor is cast as the body in a murder mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the brother of Cain was killed by him, the first murder victim in the Bible.

clue.text: Accept busy person embodies terrible evil

indicators.note: to embody is to hold within, so the busy person goes around the other part

parts.note: a busy bee is a person who is always working

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of evil are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Accepting that a hard-working person can harbour dreadful wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles evil into LIEV, and 'embodies' wraps the busy person around it, splitting it after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe a claim is to accept it as true, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Run off with one friend that's genuine

parts.note: to leg it is informal British for to run away
I is the Roman numeral for one
mate is a British word for a friend

explanation.surface: Someone who dashes away with a pal who is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG IT is British slang for running off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate is lawful and authentic, so genuine is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Pretty thing in garden's become tedious after photo

indicators.note: after puts the tedious phrase behind the photograph word

parts.note: a snap is a quick photograph
to drag on is to go on so long it becomes tedious

explanation.surface: A lovely garden has grown boring once it has been photographed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of garden's stands for 'has' and links the parts. DRAG ON comes after SNAP.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a colourful flowering plant common in gardens, an example of a pretty bloom.

clue.text: Sell loud record

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A shop pushing a noisy LP.
explanation.walkthrough: FLOG is British slang for selling something, often cheaply or hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally in Britain, to flog goods is to sell them.

clue.text: Down one last rum after dance

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters behind the dance word

parts.note: a disco is a dance or dance party

indicators.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange, so the letters of one last are made strange

explanation.surface: Knocking back one final rum once the dance is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the anagram signal, not the drink, and 'Down' means sad rather than drink it.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being unhappy, and disconsolate means deeply sad and unable to be comforted.

clue.text: Hostility shown by bowler, perhaps English

parts.note: a bowler is a kind of hat, perhaps marking an example

explanation.surface: An English bowler in cricket showing aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket, but here it is the round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility is intense dislike or enmity, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Sensitive about male emotion

indicators.note: about means going round, so the sensitive word wraps the male letter

parts.note: sentient means able to feel, hence sensitive

explanation.surface: A man who is sensitive about showing his feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the male letter sits inside the word for sensitive, before its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a feeling or tender emotion, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Wash bedding that team wants to keep?

parts.note: to clean something is to wash it
a sheet is a piece of bedding

explanation.surface: Laundering the bed linen that a sports team hopes to keep spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and other sports a team keeps this by conceding no goals; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, conceding nothing in a match is called keeping this, which a defending side always wants.

clue.text: Allow island journey? Go for it!

parts.note: to let means to allow
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A travel agent urges a customer to book that island holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom urges someone to act with full force and no holding back, like the encouragement Go for it!

clue.text: Shout about being taken in by fraud

indicators.note: being taken in by means held inside, so the fraud word encloses the about word

parts.note: a scam is a fraud or swindle
re means about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: Someone yells upon realising they have been conned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken in by' is the container signal; the surface reads it as being fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud piercing cry, so it is a kind of shout.

clue.text: Wrap run up with ailing leader in agony

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace
ailing means ill

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of agony

explanation.surface: Someone in pain, ill and running, hastily wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TROT to give TORT; 'leader in' takes the A of agony.
explanation.definitionFit: This flatbread is used to wrap fillings, and a wrap is a common name for such a filled flatbread.

clue.text: Books bishop to visit area with dreadful slum

indicators.note: to visit is to go into, so the bishop letter goes inside the rest
dreadful means in a dreadful state, so the letters of slum are knocked about

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop goes to an area with an awful slum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges SLUM to LUMS; 'to visit' puts B inside A + LUMS, after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Albums are bound books for keeping photographs, stamps or autographs, a kind of book.

clue.text: Gunners on board boat continued attack

indicators.note: on board means inside the vessel, so the gunners go into the boat word

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat
RA, the Royal Artillery, are the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Artillerymen aboard a vessel keep up their bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery is a British army regiment known as the Gunners; 'on board' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a sustained artillery bombardment, hence an attack that is kept up.

clue.text: Doctor Smooth on mission to attain heavenly body?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slick doctor heads off on an assignment to the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges SMOOTH ON. The question mark marks that the heavenly body is literally the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a project is a space mission sent to reach the Moon, the nearest celestial body.

clue.text: One's short-tempered, a result of too much sun?

definitions.meaning: a person who flares up quickly and easily loses their temper

definitions.text: a result of too much sun?
definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase describes a scalp left warm after long exposure to sunshine

explanation.surface: Someone irritable, perhaps because they sat too long in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names an impetuous, quick-tempered person, and literally describes a head heated by sunshine.

clue.text: Patch up and get married again?

definitions.meaning: to mend or fix something damaged
read as RE- plus PAIR, it is to be paired off with a spouse once more

explanation.surface: A couple mends their marriage and ties the knot again.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to fix it, and split as two parts the word also means coupling a second time.

clue.text: Uncompromising line by hospital department

parts.note: a string is a line or cord
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: A tough instruction issued by a hospital's specialist unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and exacting, allowing no compromise.

clue.text: Promise 'Road to Hell' in prime locations

indicators.note: prime locations here are the letter positions numbered by prime numbers: two, three, five and seven

explanation.surface: A vow made referencing the well-known saying that the road to hell is paved with good intentions.
explanation.walkthrough: Counting the letters of ROAD TO HELL, positions 2, 3, 5 and 7 (all prime numbers) give O, A, T and H.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise or vow.

clue.text: Shock Scot and Ulsterman on vacation

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters of Scot and Ulsterman

explanation.surface: A Scotsman and a Northern Irishman get a jolt while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties each word, leaving ST and UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or astonish them.

clue.text: Scrap coming back by motorway for test

indicators.note: coming back means the word for scrap is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to axe a plan is to scrap it
M, as in M1, is the British abbreviation for motorway

explanation.surface: A road test: a scrapyard return beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns the word for scrap round; 'Scrap' looks like a noun but is the verb to axe.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Standard moan about current legislative body

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the moan word goes round the current letter

parts.note: to lament is to moan or wail
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: The usual grumbling about the present state of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside LAMENT, after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is a national assembly that makes laws, a lawmaking body.

clue.text: Support southern banker

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: Backing a banker from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention calls a river a banker because it flows between banks, and this is an English river.

clue.text: Dear God! Man engineered the end of the world

indicators.note: engineered means constructed or contrived, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An exclamation of horror that man has brought about the apocalypse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineered' rearranges DEAR GOD MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible this is the site of the final battle, so the word now means the apocalypse.
